title: length-strata-merge: adaptive length-strata merging with KV prefetch and kernel-fit scoring
author: Maya Velankar
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive length-strata merging heuristic that reduces padding overhead and improves kernel utilization. Adds KV prefetch windowing to reduce first-token stalls for merged cohorts. Config knobs: length_strata_count, window_scaling_alpha, kv_prefetch_limit, pad_cap_percent.
body:
Context and motivation: We observed that the current bucketing/batching approaches still suffer from two practical inefficiencies in production: (1) tail sequences cause either excessive padding or underfilled kernels, and (2) first-token stalls due to KV cache misses when coalescing heterogeneous inflight requests. This PR implements a complementary heuristic — length-strata merging with adaptive windowing and a selective KV prefetch step — which aims to reduce pad overhead while improving kernel occupancy and reducing head-of-batch stalls.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): This PR adds a new scheduler pass 'LengthStrataMerger' that groups inflight requests into dynamic strata instead of static buckets. The pass computes stratified quantile boundaries from an exponential moving window of recent sequence length samples. Within each stratum we perform a greedy sliding-window merge guided by a kernel-fit scoring function that estimates effective occupancy for a target kernel (int8/float16). Before committing a merged batch, the runtime optionally issues a lightweight KV-prefetch proto that populates dispatcher-level KV entries for prefixes likely to be requested by merged candidates (configurable via kv_prefetch_limit). The merger also respects a pad_cap_percent to guarantee latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes by limiting allowed padding relative to the median sequence length in a window.

Why this is different from existing bucketers: Instead of deterministic static buckets, the strata are adaptive (quantile-driven) and the sliding merge window scales with observed variance (window_scaling_alpha). Unlike pure pad-minimization that can starve small sequences, this approach balances pad reduction with kernel-fit and tail latency via explicit constraints and a kernel-fit penalty. We also couple KV prefetching for merged cohorts to eliminate the common first-token latency spike introduced when multiple requests hit cold KV pages simultaneously.

Key files changed (high level):
- runtime/scheduler/length_strata_merger.cc (new) — core logic for quantile estimation, sliding-merge, kernel-fit scoring.
- runtime/scheduler/length_strata_merger.h (new) — public interface and config struct.
- runtime/kv/cache_prefetcher.cc (mod) — lightweight prefetch API and metrics hooks.
- runtime/config/defaults.yaml (mod) — default knobs for length_strata_count, window_scaling_alpha, kv_prefetch_limit, pad_cap_percent.
- perf/perf-canary/bench_strata_merger.py (new) — microbench harness for synthetic seqlen distributions.
- tests/scheduler/test_length_strata_merger.py (new) — unit tests for scoring and merging invariants.
- docs/ops/strata_merge.md (new) — operator-facing explanation and config guidance.

Commits (high level):
- feat: add length strata estimator and merger pass (initial impl)
- feat: integrate kernel-fit scoring and pad_cap enforcement
- feat: add KV prefetch API and connect to merger
- test: unit tests and perf-canary harness
- docs: operational runbook and config examples
- ci: flake fixes and lint adjustments

Internal API notes and knobs:
- length_strata_count (int, default 8): number of quantile strata; lower counts reduce overhead on scheduling thread.
- window_scaling_alpha (float, default 0.5): controls how much the sliding merge window grows when seqlen variance is high.
- kv_prefetch_limit (int, default 16): max number of KV entries to prefetch for a merged cohort. Prefetch is no-op when KV cache hit rate is above configured threshold.
- pad_cap_percent (float, default 30.0): maximum allowed padding ratio relative to stratum median for latency-sensitive routes (overrides full pad minimization).

Benchmarks (perf-canary summary):
We executed perf-canary runs with three synthetic mixes: short-heavy (median 16, long tail 512), bimodal (16/256), and uniform (1..1024). Key observed improvements vs baseline (existing bucketer + greedy packer):
- pad token reduction: 35% (short-heavy), 28% (bimodal), 15% (uniform)
- throughput uplift (tokens/sec): +12% (short-heavy), +9% (bimodal), +4% (uniform)
- p95 latency: improved by 7–18ms depending on mix; first-token tail reduced by ~30% on workload mixes where KV cold misses were common.
Measurement caveats: absolute numbers depend on model, sequence length distribution, and instance type. Results were gathered on G4dn-like testbed and a subset of optimizations (kernel-fit weighting) is more impactful on int8 paths.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for quantile estimator, window scaling invariants, kernel-fit scoring and pad_cap enforcement.
- Integration test in perf-canary runs (bench_strata_merger.py) added and marked flakiness-tolerant.
- CI summary: build ✅, unit tests ✅, integration (perf-canary) ✅ after 1 retry for one timing-dependent test.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):
- Elliot Chen (review): "Nice direction — kernel-fit scoring looks promising. Two asks: (1) can we make kv_prefetch opt-in per route? (2) add a guard to avoid prefetch storms when many cohorts are formed simultaneously?"
- Author (Maya): "Both addressed: prefetch is opt-in per route via config.ratelimit and we added a prefetch backoff token bucket in cache_prefetcher to limit bursts. See second commit."
- Ravi Kapoor (review): "pad_cap_percent is powerful; please add an integration test that exercises the latency-sensitive override."
- Author: "Added test_length_strata_merger_latency_override in tests; it simulates a latency-sensitive route and asserts pad ratio constraints."
- Anya Petrov (approval): "Approach wise this looks safe and the metrics hooks let ops tune behavior. Approved."

Operational notes for rollout:
- Default config kept conservative; feature is disabled for routes flagged with 'strict_latency: true' unless route opts in.
- Gradual rollout strategy suggested: enable on low-traffic staging clusters, evaluate pad_token and p95 traces, then flip on for selected non-urgent public routes.
- Expose metrics: strata_count, avg_window_width, pad_ratio_by_route, kv_prefetch_hits, kv_prefetch_failures, kernel_fit_score_histogram.

Related work and upstream links:
- ENG-1327 (Linear): Track dynamic batching failures with long-tail workloads.
- ENG-2101 (Linear): KV cache prefetch prototypes and telemetry.
- Related PRs: references to earlier packing/bucketing work were left in docs for context; this PR is intentionally incremental and interoperates with existing bucketers via runtime flags.

Merge strategy and outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and CI green. Merged as a single-change commit to keep the runtime change atomic.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Add an autoscaler-aware mode where strata sizing considers current instance utilization.
- Explore a learned kernel-fit model (small NN) instead of the heuristic scoring function used here.
- Add more perf-canary runs on low-memory/edge GPUs to tune default knobs.

If you want to validate locally: build runtime target //runtime:scheduler and run perf/perf-canary/bench_strata_merger.py with the included synthetic profiles. Configuration examples are in docs/ops/strata_merge.md.

-- CHANGELOG (short): Introduce adaptive length-strata merging with kernel-fit scoring and KV prefetch windowing to reduce padding and first-token stalls.

End of PR description.
